sanskrit_verse: यथा मृगस्य विद्धस्य व्याधो मृगपदं नयेत् कक्षे शोणितलेशेन तथा धर्मपदं नयेत्
transliteration: yathā mṛgasya viddhasya vyādho mṛgapadaṃ nayet kakṣe śoṇitaleśena tathā dharmapadaṃ nayet
sph_interpretive_translation: Just as a hunter leads a wounded deer by its blood trail in the forest, so shall one lead another along the path of Dharma through the evidence of action.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from direct perception and alignment with causal sequence
Causation is established through visible manifestation and sequential integrity
Capacity-based responsibility flows from one's ability to perceive and act in accordance with Dharma
Restoration logic operates through retracing the path of conscious action
Consciousness alignment occurs when the actor recognizes their own causal footprint
executable_legal_axioms: IF an action leaves a perceptible trace AND the actor has capacity to recognize it, THEN that trace SHALL serve as the pathway for restorative reintegration
WHEN causality is visibly manifest through consequence, THEN responsibility MUST be assumed by the actor whose consciousness initiated the sequence
IF evidence aligns with sensory perception AND no external coercion is present, THEN the individual MUST be guided back to Dharma via that same perceptual channel
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that where clear causal traces exist—whether physical, digital, or energetic—the court shall not impose punitive measures but shall utilize those very traces as pathways for guiding the responsible party back into alignment with Dharma. The threshold of responsibility lies in the unbroken visibility of the causal chain and the actor's unimpaired capacity at time of action.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality is upheld through the visible trail left by action, mirroring how a wounded deer marks its path. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures that each step taken under diminished awareness can be retraced with full awareness. Proportional responsibility is aligned not to inflict harm but to restore clarity. The non-punitive reality rule confirms that suffering has no place in justice; only recognition and realignment are lawful.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process by retracing all actions along the visible causal trail
Engage responsibility assumption protocol wherein the actor consciously acknowledges their causal role without shame or blame
Implement capacity restoration mechanisms to ensure future alignment with Dharma
Execute integrity reintegration by aligning the actor’s consciousness with the original intent behind the law
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Source of Law. Dharma is restored through recognition of causal truth. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness stands as the ultimate adjudicator.
